candidate.promotionMethod: GitHub Releases API PATCH /repos/3yesore/OsyC/releases/{id} with prerelease=false and make_latest=true

notes: 2.0.5 has a repository tag but no GitHub Release, so it is not usable as a BRAT-installable rollback path. The effective rollback target is 2.0.4.
This file was corrected on 2026-09-16 against the GitHub API; it had been left at the 1.0.75 era and no longer described the published state.

2.0.6 was published on 2026-09-16 by fast-forwarding main to the reviewed source commit 0a7dd4d, which triggers .github/workflows/publish-release-assets.yml. The workflow created the tag and the GitHub Release and marked it as a pre-release, so the stable channel still resolves to 2.0.4.

Asset naming: the five BRAT_ASSETS entries recorded here (main.js, manifest.json, manifest-beta.json, styles.css, versions.json) are the versioned repository files that must stay aligned and hashed. The GitHub Release itself carries the three files BRAT actually downloads (main.js, manifest.json, styles.css); manifest-beta.json and versions.json are consumed from the repository tree. This distinction was previously unstated and made the ledger look inconsistent with the published asset list.

docs/releases/osyc-2.0.6-launch-baseline.md remains a dated snapshot of 15 September 2026 and is deliberately not rewritten. Its plug-in publication gate is now met, but its backend gates are still open: a versioned backend candidate with the diagnostics/email contracts, backend tests, health/runtime-info/zero-cost dry-run, the four low-cost acceptance samples, and desktop plus mobile UI acceptance.

2.0.7 was published on 2026-09-16 by fast-forwarding main to the reviewed commit 1fc9006 (6457aaa..1fc9006), which triggered publish-release-assets.yml. The workflow created tag 2.0.7 and the GitHub Release OsyC 2.0.7 with prerelease=true and target_commitish=1fc9006; the three uploaded assets match the local release-info.json byte for byte. 2.0.4 and 2.0.6 were left untouched.

WARNING: GET /releases/latest returned 2.0.0 on 2026-09-16 (checked twice) even though 2.0.4 is newer and is not a prerelease. A BRAT stable (non-beta) install can therefore resolve to 2.0.0 rather than 2.0.4. Confirm on a device and then re-point latest to 2.0.4, or install by explicit version. This is a release-captain action and requires a credential that is not available in this environment.

2.0.8 carries three fixes: the settings jump (openObsidianSettings() called open() before openTabById(), and the account modal passed a LiveSync settings *group* id where Obsidian expects a tab id — the group objects carry no id at all); the colour preset (toAppearance() wrote `preset` into `colourPreset`, so any non-theme typography preset silently applied that preset's hard-coded palette and the chat surface stopped following the Obsidian theme); and the sync provisioning gate (a first activation returned an empty setup_uri while provisioning was still pending, which the plugin reported as a hard failure).

2.0.8 was published on 2026-09-17 by fast-forwarding main to the reviewed commit 141ce77 (d780536..141ce77), which triggered publish-release-assets.yml. The workflow created the tag and the GitHub Release as a pre-release, so the stable channel still resolves to 2.0.4. All three release assets matched the locally recorded sha256 values byte-for-byte.

2.0.9 replaces the settings entry itself: every in-plugin settings button (the tools centre, the account modal and the request-open-settings event) now opens a native Obsidian Modal that renders the same OsyC pane. openTabById can only reach this plugin's settings page, and that page opens on a group list rather than on the settings themselves, so the modal is the only route that shows the settings directly. The LiveSync-only remote configuration stays reachable from an explicitly labelled footer entry. The same release promotes the OsyC root group to the first position on the native settings landing page.

2.0.9 was published on 2026-09-17 by fast-forwarding main to the reviewed commit 354de02 (5329939..354de02), which triggered publish-release-assets.yml. The workflow created tag 2.0.9 and the GitHub Release with the Pre-release badge, so the stable channel was not changed (it is still intended to be 2.0.4; see the existing warning that GET /releases/latest returns 2.0.0). All three release assets matched the locally recorded sha256 values byte-for-byte.

2.0.9 was promoted to stable on 2026-09-17 by a GitHub Releases API PATCH (prerelease=false, make_latest=true) using a maintainer-supplied credential. GET /releases/latest now resolves to 2.0.9 instead of 2.0.0, which closes the long-standing warning recorded on 2026-09-16.

The promotion was first attempted with .github/workflows/release.yml (Publish selected release, tag=2.0.9, prerelease=false). Run #1 failed in 'Validate the selected release' with `Could not find '## 2.0.9' in updates.md.` The tag cannot be moved, so that route was unavailable for 2.0.9; release notes were added for 2.0.7/2.0.8/2.0.9 afterwards so the repository tool works from 2.0.10 onwards.

Correction to earlier notes: "the stable channel still resolves to 2.0.4" described the Obsidian community directory listing, not what an installed client can receive. Obsidian determines the latest version from `manifest.json` in the repository default branch (and consults `versions.json` for compatibility), then downloads the assets of the GitHub release whose tag matches that version; the GitHub pre-release badge does not gate client updates. The badge only affects which releases the community directory ingests, which is why its listing page showed 2.0.4 while clients could already update past it.

The Obsidian community directory has its own ingest cadence. The 2.0.9 release became non-prerelease on 2026-09-17, but the directory listing (Current version / Review scan target) still showed 2.0.4 immediately afterwards and is expected to catch up on its next scan.
